thread:
Maria (support): FYI just got a ticket from Acme Corp — they say ~15% of requests are 429s during peak bursts and it's happening across regions. They included this error body:

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"regional_capacity_limit","region":"us-east-1","request_id":"req_0A1B2C3D"}

Maria (support): They said it started after they ramped traffic ~10x for a marketing spike. Account is on hosted Free -> no dedicated capacity. Can someone help clarify how multi-region routing + cross-region throttles work and whether we should advise them to change retry logic / pin region?

Ashwin (eng): @Maria thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro curl and approx qps they were hitting? also org/org id so I can look up quotas. Quick question: are they forcing region in the SDK or letting our routing pick?

Maria (support): Repro from customer (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-7b","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Response header snippet they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
X-Redwood-Fallback: cross-region-throttle
X-Request-ID: req_0A1B2C3D
```
QPS reported ~35 sustained for ~5 minutes, spikes to 70 for ~30s. Org id: org_acme_42

Support Bot: New ticket created: #SUP-4829 for org_acme_42 (assigned: Maria).

Kevin (sre): Thanks Maria. Quick notes from infra side: when a region's active serving capacity for that model falls below the soft-threshold (we track per-model region_capacity) we start applying cross-region throttles to keep SLOs stable. Behavior summary:
- If request is routed to a saturated region and fallback is enabled AND a compatible replica exists in another region, router will attempt failover to that region transparently (adds X-Redwood-Fallback header).
- If failover is not possible (model mismatch, cold cache, network constraints) we return 429 with X-Redwood-Fallback: cross-region-throttle and the request_id.
- We also consume "burst credits" per org when they exceed baseline quota; once burst credits exhausted, requests are rate-limited until credits replenish (minute-level).

Kevin (sre): From logs for org_acme_42 around 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z I see repeated entries like:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] req=req_0A1B2C3D region=us-east-1 status=429 reason=regional_capacity_exceeded fallback=cross-region-throttle
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] req=req_0A1B2C3E region=eu-west-1 status=200 backend=eu-west-1-ml1 latency=45ms
[2026-03-10T14:02:40Z] org=org_acme_42 burst_credits=0 quota_consumed=1.23
```
That indicates they were getting some successful failovers but also direct 429s when fallback couldn't be satisfied or burst credits hit zero.

Ashwin (eng): Good catch. Two follow-ups: 1) Are they using session affinity/key-based routing? if they pin by session we might not be able to reroute some tokens. 2) Model compatibility: open-llama-7b has quantized variants in some regions only — if a request requires an exact variant (e.g., pinned to fp16), fallback fails. Maria can you confirm if they used model_version pin?

Maria (support): Customer says they just use model name, no explicit version pin. They use our JS SDK default settings. No session affinity as far as they reported.

Kevin (sre): Ok. Here's how to reproduce quickly (internal):
1) Use a small load generator with region override header to force us-east-1: `-H "X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1"`
2) Ramp to 60 qps for 2 minutes and watch `internal/metrics/region_capacity` and `internal/trace/log` for req ids.
3) Check admin endpoint to see burst credits: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal.redwood/api/orgs/org_acme_42/quota`
Expected admin response (sanitized):
```
{"org":"org_acme_42","burst_credits":0,"baseline_qps":20,"max_burst_qps":50}
```
If burst_credits are 0 then they will see 429s after sustained overage.

Ashwin (eng): For mitigation: we can either temporarily top up burst credits for them, or advise the customer to: 1) add exponential backoff + jitter, 2) implement client-side regional fallback by trying another region endpoint when receiving X-Redwood-Fallback header, or 3) upgrade to Dedicated or increase reserved capacity.

Maria (support): Can we top up credits as a one-off for their marketing spike? They asked to avoid upgrading right now.

Kevin (sre): I can approve a one-time 10k burst credit top-up from infra side if CS confirms. That will raise max_burst_qps to allow their 70 qps spike to succeed. Steps I'll take:
- apply temporary credit: POST https://internal.redwood/admin/quota/topup {org:org_acme_42, credits:10000, expires: "2026-03-10T18:00:00Z"}
- monitor for failed fallbacks and check for model mismatches

Ashwin (eng): Also recommend we document this behavior in the SDK docs: show X-Redwood-Fallback handling + example retry logic. Here's a quick pseudo example for JS:
```js
async function sendReq() {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) {
    const res = await fetch(url, opts);
    if (res.status === 200) return res.json();
    if (res.status === 429) {
      const fallback = res.headers.get('X-Redwood-Fallback');
      if (fallback === 'cross-region-throttle') {
        // optionally try alternate region endpoint
      }
      await sleep(Math.pow(2, attempt) * 100 + jitter());
      continue;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries');
}
```

Support Bot: Action queued: top-up request created (admin-op-991).

Emily (cs): looping in CS — I'll ask Acme if they want the top-up and offer a short trial of Dedicated. Maria can you ping me offline with the ticket link? :+1:

Maria (support): Pinged customer for confirmation. Also added example curl for region-based retry to the ticket. Thanks all — I'll update the ticket once CS confirms and Kevin applies the top-up.

Kevin (sre): Once top-up applied I'll post the admin-op id and the time window here. Also logging note: we should add a clearer header like `X-Redwood-Burst-Remaining` to help customers introspect in real time. Filing a follow-up doc ticket.

Ashwin (eng): Cool. If we see repeated pattern across customers we should consider changing fallback behavior to prefer cross-region failover whenever compatible model exists (even if cold) or provide an opt-in for customer to allow cold-fallback. I'll open RFC backlog item.

Maria (support): Closing loop for now; will reopen if the top-up doesn't resolve. Thanks everyone :)
